name: toolsmith-ci-wait
intent: Wait for the CI runs of one commit to finish, printing only what failed.
usage: toolsmith-ci-wait [--pr N | --commit SHA] [--timeout MINUTES] [--interval SECONDS] [--lines N]
use_when: You pushed and need the CI result before the next step (merge, release, reply).
You would otherwise poll with `gh pr checks`, `gh run list`, `gh run watch` and sleep, or read failures with `gh run view --log-failed | grep`.
not_for: Starting or re-running CI: use `gh run rerun`.
CI systems other than GitHub Actions.
Reading a whole job log: use `gh run view <id> --log`.
input: No stdin. By default the commit is HEAD, which must be pushed; --commit names another commit (SHA or ref), --pr N uses the head commit of pull request N. Runs in the current repository's directory and talks to GitHub through `gh`, so `gh` must be installed and signed in.

options.text: Wait for the head commit of this pull request number.
Wait for this commit (SHA or ref) instead of HEAD.
Give up after this many minutes (default 30). The first run must appear within 2 minutes.
Log lines to show per failed job (default 40).

output: When every run passed: 'CI for <sha>: N runs, all passed.' and one line per run. When something failed: a line per job of every run with its conclusion, then for each failed job its last log lines (from `gh run view --log-failed`, with timestamps and colours removed) under '== <job>: last N log lines =='. Nothing is printed while waiting.

exit_codes.text: Every run finished and passed (success, skipped or neutral).
A run failed or was cancelled; the failed jobs and their logs are shown. Also used when gh is missing or fails.
No result: HEAD is not pushed, no run appeared within 2 minutes, or runs were still going at the timeout.

examples.title: Every run passed
examples.situation: Two workflows ran on the commit and both passed.
examples.stdout:
CI for 7e6179a: 2 runs, all passed.
  success   Test
  success   Lint

examples.title: Waits while a run is in progress, then shows the failed job's log
examples.situation: The Test workflow is still running at the first check; it then fails in one of its two jobs.

fake_commands.gh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
state="$(dirname "$0")/calls"
case "$1 $2" in
  "run list")
    n=$(cat "$state" 2>/dev/null || echo 0); echo $((n + 1)) > "$state"
    if [ "$n" = 0 ]; then echo '[{"databaseId":201,"name":"Test","status":"in_progress","conclusion":""}]'
    else echo '[{"databaseId":201,"name":"Test","status":"completed","conclusion":"failure"}]'; fi ;;
  "run view")
    if [ "$4" = "--json" ]; then echo '{"jobs":[{"name":"Linux, Ruby 4.0","conclusion":"failure"},{"name":"macOS","conclusion":"success"}]}'
    else
      j='Linux, Ruby 4.0	Run bin/test	'
      printf "${j}\357\273\2772026-10-07T20:25:06.7478892Z   1) Failure:\n"
      printf "${j}2026-10-07T20:25:06.7480034Z HistoryTest#test_never_overwrites [test/history_test.rb:261]:\n"
      printf "${j}2026-10-07T20:25:06.7483019Z Expected: 1\n"
      printf "${j}2026-10-07T20:25:06.7483715Z \033[31m  Actual: 0\033[0m\n"
      printf "${j}2026-10-07T20:25:06.7484645Z 96 runs, 818 assertions, 1 failures, 0 errors, 0 skips\n"
    fi ;;
  *) echo "fake gh: unexpected $*" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

examples.title: HEAD is not pushed
examples.situation: A repository with one local commit and no remote.
examples.setup:
set -e
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=Dev GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=dev@example.com GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=Dev GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=dev@example.com
git init -q .
git commit -q --allow-empty -m Start
examples.stderr_regex: \Atoolsmith-ci-wait: HEAD \([0-9a-f]{7}\) is not on any remote branch, so CI cannot have run on it\. Push it first\.\n\z
examples.stderr_sample: toolsmith-ci-wait: HEAD (1a2b3c4) is not on any remote branch, so CI cannot have run on it. Push it first.
